21|Geothermal Cascade Utilisation|Recover usable heat in successive stages rather than discarding warm geothermal water after one application.

22|Cascade Utilisation Flow Diagram|Production well → high-temperature uses, 80-60°C: thermal driving of liquid-desiccant dehumidification, bathing-pool heating and domestic hot-water heating → intermediate uses, ≤60°C: play-pool make-up water and temperature maintenance, low-temperature make-up water heating and floor/air-conditioning heating → low-temperature uses, 40-20°C: water-source heat-pump recovery and heating → reinjection, ≤20°C. Temperature bands are illustrative source values, not fixed design setpoints.

23|Water-Source Heat-Pump Operation|Electrical input enables a heat pump to transfer low-grade source heat to a higher useful temperature. Cooling: compressor → condenser, rejecting heat to groundwater/cooling water → expansion valve → evaporator, absorbing heat from building chilled water → compressor. Heating: the condenser heats building water; the expansion valve reduces refrigerant pressure; the evaporator extracts source-water heat; vapour returns to the compressor.

45|Geothermal Scale Control|Scale formation, removal methods, equipment and chemical dosing references.

46|Why Geothermal Systems Scale|Calcium, silica, magnesium and iron, plus dissolved CO₂, oxygen and H₂S, may be present in geothermal fluids. Pressure, temperature and gas changes can cause precipitation. Source lists calcium carbonate, calcium silicate, silica, calcite and barite deposits. Hardened deposits restrict flow and production. Deposit and water analysis inform treatment.

47|Scale Formation - Flow Diagram|Geothermal fluid rises → pressure/temperature change. Pressure falls → CO₂ release → pH rises → carbonate concentration rises → supersaturated calcium carbonate precipitates → pipe-wall scale. Temperature falls → silica solubility falls → silicic-acid polymerisation → colloidal silica deposition → scale. Corrosion products/microorganisms provide nucleation sites. Key: CO₂逸出 = CO₂ release; 硅酸聚合 = silicic-acid polymerisation; 附着管壁成垢 = pipe-wall deposition; 提供成核位点 = provide nucleation sites.

48|Treatment Decision Flowchart - Source Mismatch|Source title says scale removal, but the internal diagram concerns corrosion. Full flow: water analysis → dominant corrosion cause. Dissolved oxygen → oxygen scavenger + passivator. Chloride/H₂S → adsorbing imidazoline + molybdate. Low-temperature acidic water → neutraliser + organic amine. High-temperature alkaline water → dispersing scale inhibitor + zinc salt. Dynamic dosing → corrosion coupons + electrochemical monitoring → corrosion rate ≤0.1 mm/year? Yes: effective; no: adjust blend/dose. Source options are not validated chemical prescriptions.

51|Corrosion Mechanisms|Four interacting contributors: electrochemical corrosion in conductive water, chloride/sulphide attack on passive films; acidic species associated with CO₂/H₂S; oxygen ingress and differential-aeration/crevice attack; and microbiologically influenced corrosion. Temperature, salinity, gases, oxygen and microbiology must be assessed together. Numerical temperature/rate generalisations in the source are not universal design rules.
